plan.vision: A strict Spec Roadmap detailing the exact Agentic problem, atomic milestones, and Testing Strategy. The project aims to create a security-focused agent that monitors and enforces secure coding practices in real-time. Atomic milestones include: 1) Define core security rules and policies, 2) Implement real-time code analysis, 3) Integrate with existing IDEs, 4) Develop a robust testing suite, 5) Document and release.

code_flow_security_agent.py: def enforce_rules(code: str, rules: list) -> bool

plan.lessons_learned: This project avoids past mistakes by using memory-mapped files for efficient data handling, prioritizing algorithmic efficiency over OOP overhead, and ensuring that all dependencies are pinned in a virtual environment. The repository will be kept lightweight by excluding heavy directories with .gitignore, and clear setup scripts will be provided for reproducibility. Additionally, the project will focus on security and isolation, ensuring that the code executed within the sandbox cannot access or modify external resources. There are no hidden paid-API dependencies.
plan.commit_message: Implement a security-focused agent that monitors and enforces secure coding practices in real-time.

files_to_generate.instructions: This file contains the main logic for analyzing and enforcing security rules. It should include functions `analyze_code` which takes a string of code and returns a dictionary of security issues, and `enforce_rules` which takes a string of code and a list of rules, and returns a boolean indicating if the code passes all rules.

This file defines the security rules and policies. It should include functions `get_security_rules` which returns a list of predefined security rules, and `add_rule` which adds a new rule to the list.

This file handles integration with various IDEs. It should include functions `integrate_with_ide` which takes an IDE name and integrates the agent with it, and `get_supported_ides` which returns a list of supported IDEs.

This file contains the unit tests for the project. It should import and use the actual generated modules to test the core logic. The tests must cover all functions in `code_flow_security_agent.py`, `security_rules.py`, and `ide_integration.py`.
This file should ignore venv, __pycache__, and .env files to keep the repository lightweight.
This file should explain the architecture of the project, including the purpose of each file, how to set up and run the project, and any other relevant information.
